title: Independently audit staged544 terminal-to-owner cost bridge
body:
## Result

Independently corroborate PR[3945](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3945)'s terminal-to-owner cost bridge at `91f81d131252db704f945891da1ea54e29d46b8b`. Both providers freshly reproduce the local invoice; all 1,321,920 literal roles and 725,760 physical bins are checked. Exactly 84,240 bins absorb one promoted terminal dimension. The complete paid delta is `51840 H1 - 42120 H2 - 19440 H3 + 22680 H4`, with zero rank-mass change and the claimed complete profile `{1:8041680,2:2306880,3:729648,4:353160,5:69120,8:25920,48:137952}`. No discrepancy was found in this scoped bridge. No new construction or kappa is claimed.

The checker imports no predecessor code. It uses explicit binary point sets for the full local invoice, exact interleaved free-program identity, reverse source-window queries and coordinate bitmaps for physical bins. It connects widths derived from actual terminal/entrance subspaces to the actual dispatch and idle remainder bill; it does not trust word report histograms. Exact program identity establishes relative abstract scalar/permutation equality on arbitrary dirty inputs and private buffers. Native Gaussian/Clifford phases remain excluded from that statement.

## Reproduction and validation

Only `research/staged544-terminal-owner-bridge-audit/` changes: 20 files, 359,268 bytes. Default registered replay retains four exact words (294,388 bytes) and freshly checks both local providers plus 11 semantic rejecting controls in normal and optimized Python. It deliberately prints `PASS_LOCAL_BRIDGE_ONLY`: a default CI pass is not a fresh literal-owner audit.

The full owner replay uses 12 explicit immutable public inputs fetched into a fresh directory by `fetch_sources.py`; every byte is SHA256-pinned and checked again by the verifier. Both final full runs passed: 62.033 seconds normal and 50.446 seconds optimized on Python 3.12.3, with exact retained-result equality and all source bytes unchanged. All 17 mathematical controls reject, including six through the actual owner production audit: changed identity, family collision, closed window, shifted offset, missing dispatch and complete-bill mismatch. Four additional production CLI controls reject a corrupted source and stale retained receipt in normal/optimized Python. Official registered local replay passed in 5.100 seconds. Commands, hashes, scope and complete cost-status ledger are retained.

This is a deliberate independent audit of Dugongue's changed-terminal construction. PR[3941](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3941)/[3942](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3942)/[3957](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3957) fixed-exit retiming results do not admit that change. Canonical main `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90` and priority revision 6 were refreshed unchanged; bounded Discussions and complete 662-open-PR-body pagination were checked. [Active audit claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3945#issuecomment-6261600388). No exhaustive novelty claim.

Fresh native phase recipes, complete ordinary/outer release, a new root calculation, all-size compiler, physical hosting implementation, precision/stock/tape/recovery, analytic and BIT assumptions remain unverified here. Unknown costs are not zero; the selected frontier is unchanged. The next bounded audit is the changed native phase/interface and its source-bound release admission.

Apache-2.0. No independent human or proof-kernel review is claimed.

## Frozen publication checks

GitHub-authored scientific commit `6ff67539f1131a287eb9a9a98bf1e94a02eecba7`, one parent at canonical main. All 20 committed files match local validated bytes, and the declared Git provenance passes the source-history gate. The official committed package export passes integrity checking; its Git-free local replay passes in normal and optimized Python with unchanged exported bytes. Hosted CI status is separate and is not preclaimed here.
